contexts.text: The servant ran to meet her () = exploration from Divine good. Explained.
The girl ran () = the propensity or animus of that affection.
Laban ran out unto the man () = the animus of the affection of good towards truth.
She ran and told her father () = acknowledgement through interior truths. To run and tell = the affection of making known; here, from acknowledgement.
He ran to meet him () = agreement.
Those of this province run about hither and thither.
Esau ran to meet him () = the influx of Divine natural good.
To run with a thief () = to alienate truth from one's self through falsity.
To run to war () = the ardour of fighting. AE 558.
On punishment by a running round.
To run about () = to go astray.
